assigned.title: Critical E2E harness
assigned.acceptance: Catalog to title to player to progress fixture journey is reproducible in CI. MANDATORY ADDITION 2026-09-19, at gpt-architect's round-50 direction when it approved PL-0707, and placed here because THIS TASK OWNS e2e/**: expectedStatus in e2e/src/contract.ts must recognise request_body_too_large as HTTP 413; an E2E case must drive an oversized request and verify 413 PLUS the reason code; and THE E2E HELPER MUST REMAIN INDEPENDENTLY RESTATED rather than importing the server's status function. That last clause is the point of the whole item and must not be optimised away: the helper is a deliberately hand-written mirror, and importing playbackSessionHttpStatus would make the assertion a tautology that passes however wrong the server is. Today the helper derives request-level denials from only request_malformed and request_field_not_permitted, so it would infer 403 where the server correctly answers 413. Nothing fails yet, because no e2e spec sends an oversized body -- the mirror is simply out of date from f83bc65 onward, which is the failure mode a mirror has.

e2e.evidence: EXECUTED, in the CI job's own configuration, on e24d51f. Commands, run from e2e/ with PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH and PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD unset so the PINNED revision resolves from Playwright's default cache, CI=1, and the three variables .github/workflows/ci.yml sets on the e2e job (CONTENT_RIGHTS_ENFORCEMENT=strict, LIBERTY_FC_SEED=20250819, LIBERTY_FIXTURE_MEDIA_ORIGIN=https://fixtures.invalid): (1) LIBERTY_E2E_WEB_MODE=production npm test -- --project=api --project=chromium -> 61 passed, 12 skipped, 0 failed, exit 0; (2) LIBERTY_E2E_WEB_MODE=development npm test -- --project=api --project=chromium -> 70 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed, exit 0. BOTH MODES, because docs/E2E.md makes the pair the gate: the strings production requires absent are the ones development requires present. Browser: chromium 1234 (Chrome for Testing 151.0.7922.34) from /root/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium-1234, which is the revision e2e/package-lock.json's @playwright/test 1.62.1 pins -- NOT the 1194 substitution the 2026-09-15 evidence was caveated for. retries=0, forbidOnly on. THE REAL JOURNEY RAN: critical-journey.spec.ts executed 10 chromium tests in each mode covering home -> title -> play affordance -> watch route -> player page -> back to catalog, alongside progress.api.spec.ts, catalog.api.spec.ts, search.spec.ts and rights-boundary.api.spec.ts. No unit test, typecheck, build or file-existence claim is offered in place of any of it. THE PL-0707 REQUIREMENT IS IMPLEMENTED AND DRIVEN: three new api-project tests, green in both modes -- 'an oversized body is refused unread, with 413 and a size reason' (asserts status 413, outcome denied, request_body_too_large as the PRIMARY reason, and that the refusal echoes none of the padding), 'a body just under the cap is not refused for its size' (the pairing that stops the first passing against a route that refuses everything), and 'the status mapping this suite checks against is not the server's own' (reads src/contract.ts and fails if any module specifier reaches @liberty, apps/web or the session contract, or if playbackSessionHttpStatus is ever called). NON-VACUITY PROVEN BY MUTATION: replacing the 413 branch with a no-op makes the oversized spec fail 'Expected: 403 / Received: 413' at the decision() status cross-check, exit 1; restored and typechecked clean. SCOPE LIMIT STATED: api and chromium only, exactly the pair the CI job runs. WebKit, mobile-safari and Firefox were NOT launched and this result claims nothing about them; 12 skips in production and 3 in development are the mode-guarded and media-rig-guarded cases. This is a local container run, not a GitHub runner.

assigned.notes: INHERITED INPUT, recorded before the claim on gpt-architect's round-45 instruction: "PL-0701 should remain dependency-gated until its other prerequisites are satisfied, but it inherits the Round 45 E2E files as pre-existing input and its provenance record should state that when claimed." Round 45 wrote a substantial part of e2e/** under PL-0501, not under this task, because this task was dependency-blocked behind PL-0501 and could not legally be claimed to produce the evidence PL-0501's review required; the reviewer authorised that overlap in advance and accepted it at 97011e71008fe69445845debb879534895cdc754. INHERITED FROM PREDECESSORS AND DELIBERATELY NOT CLAIMED, which is the distinction that stops this task from appearing to have written a predecessor's work: 1d26451 'PL-0501 round 45' created playback-session.desktop.api.spec.ts, playback-session.cross-target.api.spec.ts, src/backend-stub.mjs and src/tls.ts; 719d2d7 'Nine lanes' created src/progress-contract.ts and tests/progress.api.spec.ts; 34c16c9 'PL-0204/PL-0501' created e2e/package-lock.json. The handler this suite exercises is a reviewDependency rather than a write surface. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE E2E CONCURRENCY FINDING, answered on the evidence rather than on convenience: PL-0701 does NOT own e2e/tests/playback-session.desktop.api.spec.ts. Its entire history is one commit, 1d26451, which is PL-0501's. The reviewer's instruction was to fold the concurrency correction in ONLY IF PL-0701 legally owns the file, and it does not, so the correction is NOT made here and the finding stays open for whichever task owns that spec.

recommended.title: A repo guard that times out under load is a guard nobody can read
recommended.acceptance: packages/media-inspection/src/net-policy-boundary.test.ts:396, the test named “is not restated by any file outside this package”, stops being a test whose result depends on machine load and on what is on disk, WITHOUT weakening the property it asserts. THE DEFECT, DIAGNOSED RATHER THAN NAMED. Its failure mode is 'Error: Test timed out in 5000ms', not an assertion failure -- the assertion has never reported a false offender; the test simply does not finish. Its listSourceFiles recurses into every directory under packages/ and apps/ with NO exclusions and reads every .ts file it finds: 3,680 files totalling 24.3 MB on the tree measured, of which 3,337 are under node_modules and the rest include build output. The set of files the property is actually about is 327, reachable in 1-2 ms once node_modules, .next, .turbo, dist and coverage are skipped. It is the only test in this repository whose runtime is a function of installed dependencies and build artifacts rather than of source, which is why it presents as intermittent: every other repo-walking guard here -- packages/net-policy/src/module-boundary.test.ts, packages/contracts/src/module-boundary.test.ts, packages/provider-sdk/src/stremio/net-policy-boundary.test.ts and apps/web/src/app/watch/route-loading-boundaries.test.ts -- is scoped to its own SRC_DIR or APP_DIRECTORY. THE REPRODUCTION GRADIENT, measured on 2026-09-22 at e24d51f on a 2-core container: the test body alone, idle with a warm page cache, 109 ms; the whole file in an isolated vitest run, 687 ms; the file under turbo run test --force with a warm cache, 849-995 ms; the same under turbo run test --force immediately after dropping the page cache, 3,048 ms. The observed failure happened on a run started immediately after the e2e suite had rewritten apps/web/.next and apps/web/dist/desktop -- thousands of freshly written files, a cold cache, background flushing, and up to nine other workspace vitest processes competing for two cores -- which is where that gradient crosses the 5,000 ms default testTimeout. REQUIRED: the walk must not descend into node_modules, .next, .turbo, dist or coverage, and the exclusion list must be stated with its reason rather than left as a magic array. REQUIRED: the property must not be narrowed to buy the speed -- it must still see every source file under packages/ and apps/ outside this package, and the implementer must show that a planted offender is still caught. A RAISED testTimeout IS NOT AN ACCEPTABLE FIX ON ITS OWN: it moves the ceiling without removing the dependence on disk state, and the next person to add a dependency moves the runtime again. SECOND DEFECT, FOUND WHILE DIAGNOSING AND IN SCOPE: build output ALREADY contains the string this test looks for. Seven files under apps/web/.next and apps/web/dist/desktop carry a reference-path fragment naming m3u8-parser.d.ts inside bundled chunks. They are .js today so the .ts filter misses them, which means the test is one bundler-output change away from naming a build artifact as an offender and failing for a reason that has nothing to do with any source file. The exclusion above fixes the correctness hazard and the performance one with the same edit, which is the argument for doing it that way rather than by raising a timeout.
recommended.notes: Filed 2026-09-22 by claude-test while executing PL-0504's and PL-0701's gates. THIS IS THE FINDING gpt-architect ORDERED PRESERVED AND EXPLICITLY ORDERED NOT TO BE CALLED A FLAKE, at the round-73 verdict: 'Do not label that failure a flake. Preserve the finding and investigate on its next occurrence as previously directed.' This is that next occurrence, and the investigation is in the acceptance. The first occurrence, during PL-0503's gates, could not name the failing test because the capture grep discarded it; that was reported at the time as a capture error, not as a flake. This occurrence was captured in full: src/net-policy-boundary.test.ts > the m3u8-parser shim is referenced from the file that imports it > is not restated by any file outside this package. The earlier working hypothesis -- 2 cores, turbo concurrency 10, and this package having no vitest.config.ts unlike packages/contracts -- was partly right and insufficient. Contention is a necessary condition, not the cause. The cause is that the test reads 24.3 MB it has no reason to read, so its runtime tracks page-cache state and build-artifact volume, and contention only decides which side of the 5 s ceiling that lands on. Three full-monorepo runs on the same tree after the failure were green (252/252 in this package), which is exactly why a load-dependent test must not be judged by re-running it. packages/media-inspection/vitest.config.ts is in allowedPaths because the implementer may conclude the package needs one; that is a decision for the implementer and this task does not require it. apps/web/src/app/api/v1/playback/build-target.test.ts is in reviewDependencies rather than allowedPaths: it resolves a REPO_ROOT and walks directories too, so it is worth checking for the same shape, but nothing observed implicates it and widening this task to it would be a guess.
